items.title: Use a password manager with a unique password per site
items.detail: Bitwarden, 1Password, or KeePassXC. Reused passwords are how one breach becomes ten. Generate + store, don't memorise.

items.title: Turn on two-factor auth everywhere it's offered
items.detail: Prefer an authenticator app or hardware key over SMS.

items.title: Switch to passkeys where available
items.detail: Phishing-resistant and nothing to leak in a breach.

items.title: Drop SMS 2FA where an app/key option exists
items.detail: SMS codes are defeated by SIM-swapping. Keep SMS only as a last-resort backup.

items.title: Save backup/recovery codes offline
items.detail: Print them or store in your password manager's secure notes — not in plain email.

items.title: Review active sessions & connected apps
items.detail: On Google, Microsoft, Apple, Meta, X: revoke old devices and third-party app grants you don't recognise.

items.title: Change passwords flagged as breached or reused
items.detail: Start with email + bank + anything sharing that password.

items.title: Lock down your primary email with strong 2FA
items.detail: Whoever controls your inbox can reset everything else. Treat it as the crown jewels.

items.title: Use aliases / plus-addressing for signups
items.detail: you+shop@gmail.com, or a relay so leaks don't expose your real address.

items.title: Audit inbox forwarding rules & filters
items.detail: Attackers add silent auto-forward rules after a compromise. Delete any you didn't create.

items.title: Stop using one email for everything
items.detail: Separate high-value (bank, gov) from throwaway signups so a marketing leak can't reach your bank login.

items.title: Set a carrier port-out PIN / SIM lock
items.detail: Call your carrier and add a transfer PIN — the main defence against SIM-swap account takeover.

items.title: Use a secondary/VoIP number for signups & 2FA
items.detail: Keeps your real number off marketing lists and people-search sites.

items.title: Enable full-disk encryption
items.detail: BitLocker (Windows) or FileVault (Mac). A lost laptop shouldn't equal a data breach.

items.title: Keep OS, browser, and apps auto-updating
items.detail: Most real-world compromise is unpatched software, not zero-days.

items.title: Short auto-lock + biometric/PIN on every device
items.detail: 1-2 minute lock on phone and laptop.

items.title: Use a filtering resolver / VPN on untrusted networks
items.detail: NextDNS or Quad9 for DNS-level blocking; a reputable VPN on public Wi-Fi.

items.title: Install a content/tracker blocker
items.detail: uBlock Origin cuts trackers and malvertising.

items.title: Block third-party cookies
items.detail: On by default in Firefox/Safari; enable it in Chrome's privacy settings.

items.title: Enable Global Privacy Control
items.detail: A legally-recognised 'do not sell/share' signal in some states.

items.title: Turn off ad personalisation
items.detail: Google (adssettings.google.com) and Meta (accountscenter) both let you disable interest-based ads.

items.title: Freeze your credit — Equifax
items.detail: Blocks new-account fraud; free and reversible.

items.title: Freeze your credit — Experian
items.detail: Do all three bureaus for full coverage.

items.title: Freeze your credit — TransUnion
items.detail: The third of the three US bureaus.

items.title: Opt out of pre-approved credit offers
items.detail: Cuts junk mail and a common identity-theft vector.

items.title: Work through the data-broker opt-outs
items.detail: The single biggest reduction in what strangers can look up.

items.title: Delete accounts you no longer use
items.detail: Every dormant account is future breach exposure.

items.title: Search yourself regularly
items.detail: Set a monthly reminder to run the self-search and re-scan.

items.title: Lock down social-media privacy settings
items.detail: Set profiles to private/friends; remove birth year, phone, and address from public view.

items.title: Disable 'find me by phone/email' on social platforms
items.detail: Stops your account being tied to a leaked number/email. Check Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn.
